points.description: States one valid advantage of reservoir flood routing: it estimates peak reservoir levels (or outflow/storage) during a flood, which helps design/size overflow channels or spillways so nearby areas are not submerged.
points.partial_credit: Half if only a vague benefit is given (e.g. 'helps predict reservoir behaviour in floods') without peak level or the use for spillway/overflow design.

points.description: States one valid advantage of channel flood routing: it gives the flood profile (stage/discharge variation with time or duration) along the channel during a storm, which helps design bridges, control transport, or plan bank-side development.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'helps predict flood in the river') without the flood profile/duration or a use such as bridges, transport or bank development.

rubric.notes: Full marks need one correct advantage for each type, reservoir and channel, with the key idea (peak level for overflow design; flood profile over time for bridges, transport or bank development). Give part marks for a vague or half-stated advantage. Give no marks for a wrong or unrelated advantage, or a definition of routing with no advantage. If the two answers are swapped or mixed up, do not credit the mixed one.
